## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nandakattheragāthā* (Thag 4.4) is a short poetic text located in the *Catukkanipāta* (Book of the Fours) of the *Theragāthā*, within the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Tipiṭaka [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. Attributed to the elder (thera) Nandaka, the poem consists of four verses [Catalog; DharmaNexus]. On SuttaCentral, nine translations in eight modern languages are recorded, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

No direct external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are noted by SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus records Pali-internal text reuse exclusively with the text's commentary, the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (*Dutiyo bhāgo*), which quotes and comments upon the verses across segments 0.4–4.5 [DharmaNexus].
